test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 23 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The All-India Kisan Sabha was founded in Lucknow in April _______ with Swami Sahjanand Saraswati as the president.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1936**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All-India Kisan Sabha** (AIKS) was founded in **April 1936** at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The formation of AIKS was driven by the need to address issues concerning **land rights, rural exploitation, and agrarian reforms.**
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**, a prominent leader of farmers and peasants, was elected as the first president of the AIKS.
 
• The Sabha aimed to mobilize farmers, peasants, and agricultural workers for their **socio-economic and political rights**.
 
• It became closely associated with the **Indian National Congress** and played a significant role in the **freedom struggle**.
 
• The organization was instrumental in various **peasant movements**, particularly in regions like Bihar, Bengal, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• One of its key objectives was to abolish the **zamindari system** and secure fair land distribution for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**__

 __
 
• He was a prominent leader of the **peasant movement** in India and is often referred to as the **founder of the Kisan Sabha movement.**
 
• Sahajanand Saraswati authored several books, including **'Mera Jeevan Sangharsh' (My Life Struggle)**, which outlines his experiences and struggles for farmers' rights.
 
• He advocated for the abolition of the **zamindari system** and equal rights for peasants.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**__
 
 
• The **Indian National Congress (INC)** was the principal leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• The INC provided a platform for the formation of several organizations, including the **All-India Kisan Sabha**, to address specific societal and economic issues.
 
• Its session in **Lucknow (1936)** was significant as it highlighted the necessity of addressing rural and agrarian problems.
